threatModel.summary: Jubarte processes untrusted DOCX/OOXML, Markdown, and legacy DOC into document views, edited packages, tracked-change redlines, PDF/PNG, and reports. The Rust engine is consumed by its native CLI, PyO3 Python APIs/CLI, and wasm-bindgen browser/Node APIs and Node CLI. Python additionally provides a stdio MCP server with explicit directory-capability document/artifact I/O. Native rendering also performs ambient font discovery and font-index persistence, so the engine is not universally filesystem-pure. The optional native self-update command downloads a GitHub release and replaces the executable; release automation separately holds publication/signing authority. findings.title: Rendering renamed auxiliary XML parts can exhaust the process stack
findings.summary: A document author can point internal numbering, fontTable, theme, styles or settings relationships at deeply nested XML under non-XML filenames. Admission skips XML policy on those auxiliary filenames, but the concrete renderer consumers parse them recursively, allowing a compact DOCX to terminate conversion.

severity.rationale: Attacker-controlled document data deterministically bypasses the depth policy and can abort a local conversion or an embedding worker. Exposure is constrained to a caller choosing to process that document; no remote service or cross-tenant deployment is established, and SECURITY.md recommends process CPU/memory limits.
severity.changeConditions: A shared service accepting public document uploads without per-job process isolation would increase operational impact; enforcing XML limits at each semantic consumer removes this path.

confidence.rationale: Static trace connects the extension-based admission decision, relationship-selected numbering part and unchecked recursive parser. No runtime trigger was executed.

rootCause.summary: `admit()` classifies XML by filename and only adds a nonstandard-extension exception for the main part. `main_rel_part()` trusts internal relationship targets, so `load_numbering()` can select an auxiliary `.bin` part. `parse_numbering_xml()` invokes the permissive DOM parser, whose element recursion has no depth limit, without validating the selected bytes. Independently checked fontTable, theme, styles and settings consumers repeat this relationship-to-unchecked-parser path; the same extension-based admission control fails for each.

findings.remediation: Apply the active XML depth/tag limits to every relationship-selected part immediately before DOM parsing, regardless of filename, and use bounded or iterative parsing as defense in depth.

limitations: No malicious file was generated or executed.
Other auxiliary XML consumers have not been exhaustively enumerated.

findings.title: Importing a cyclic drawing payload can terminate Markdown conversion
findings.summary: A Markdown author can supply a `drawing:` image payload with a dependency that points to itself. JSON decoding accepts that graph and package assembly recursively materializes it without tracking visited dependencies, exhausting the conversion process stack.

severity.rationale: A small attacker-supplied Markdown image payload can abort a caller processing it, including native or WASM conversion. This is a constrained document-processing availability failure; remote multi-user deployment is not established and process quotas are a caller obligation.
severity.changeConditions: A shared unisolated Markdown conversion service would increase impact; rejecting cycles or memoizing in-progress parts removes the deterministic trigger.

confidence.rationale: Independent source trace verifies direct public Markdown acceptance, unvalidated dependency indices, and recursive traversal with no cycle guard; no application code was executed.

codeEvidence.label: Public Markdown conversion
codeEvidence.explanation: The public API accepts the caller's Markdown, including drawing destinations.

codeEvidence.label: Drawing destination decoded without graph validation
codeEvidence.explanation: Base64 JSON becomes Drawing with caller-selected dependency indices; deserialization supplies no graph traversal control.

codeEvidence.label: Decoded drawing enters the output model
codeEvidence.explanation: The writer accepts a drawing URL and stores the decoded structure for package assembly.

codeEvidence.label: Package assembly walks root dependencies
codeEvidence.explanation: An internal relationship with a valid dependency index invokes dep_part.

codeEvidence.label: Dependency traversal recurses before recording a completed part
codeEvidence.explanation: The function records only chosen output names and recursively follows valid inner indices without visited or in-progress graph state.

codeEvidence.label: Package emitter calls materialize
codeEvidence.explanation: Package emission passes the attacker-supplied Drawing to the recursive materializer.

rootCause.summary: `picture()` accepts a decoded `Drawing` from caller-controlled Markdown and package assembly invokes `materialize()`. Root relationships select dependency indices. `dep_part()` inserts a generated filename into `used`, but does not mark the dependency index as in progress or completed before following its relationships. A self-edge therefore re-enters the same dependency indefinitely; filename collision handling does not stop the graph recursion.

findings.remediation: Validate and bound the drawing dependency graph before assembly; use a per-index in-progress/completed map to reject cycles or allocate each output part once before resolving links.

limitations: No crafted input was generated or executed.
A valid captured graph cycle may also reproduce this, but the proven path is author-supplied Markdown.
validation.summary: Verified a single dependency with `rels[].part` pointing to its own valid index passes the only index checks. `dep_part()` recursively invokes itself before writing/comparing the part bytes. Capture-time MAX_DEPS and JSON nesting limits do not constrain this flat cyclic graph, and no graph validation is performed by decode().

dataflow.outcome: stack exhaustion and process or WASM-instance termination

likelihood.why: Requires the victim to import the attacker's Markdown; no public service is assumed.

reachability.summary: Any consumer of the public Markdown-to-DOCX API that converts a document from a lower-trust author can trigger the path with default options; no local file or network access is required.

attackPath.summary: Pass Markdown containing a `drawing:` image URL whose decoded root relationship points to dependency 0 and whose dependency 0 relationship points back to 0 to `markdown_to_docx()`.

Import a shared acyclic dependency graph and assert each part is emitted once.

findings.title: Redaction checks can approve documents that retain the secret in UTF-16 XML
findings.summary: A document can keep a copy of redacted text in a UTF-16 XML part. The leak checker decodes XML parts as UTF-8, misses that copy, and can approve clean/redline outputs that still disclose the supposedly removed text.

severity.rationale: Sensitive content can remain readable in an output approved for sharing. This requires a UTF-16 XML copy and subsequent distribution; no broader secret store, remote service or high-impact data class is assumed.
severity.changeConditions: Evidence of high-impact sensitive data or a shared unisolated service processing public input would increase the rating; enforcing the stated invariant or removing its prerequisites would reduce it.

findings.remediation: Decode XML according to its supported encoding before semantic leak checking, reusing the admission transcoder; fail closed on undecodable/unparseable parts and check supported raw encodings as defense in depth.

Real deployment and process quotas remain unknown.
